records.choice: Role: APPLY — the Academy ownership doctrine applied to one dated fact (1.2B weekly ChatGPT users, Altman, DevDay, Sep 29 2026). Objective (catalogue, GROUNDED, 16 words): 'Show 1.2 billion weekly users rent AI access while owning none of the layer around it.' Payoff schedule (H4): the number lands first (L2), repetition makes it a habit (L3), the turn is planted at L4 ('the part nobody counts' → RENTS IT), the mechanism is shown at L5 (the chat box = the thinnest harness), and the equation pays off at L6: ADOPTION TOTAL / OWNERSHIP ZERO. The bridge (DR-BRIDGE) then spends the conviction the payoff earned.
records.alternatives: INTRODUCE (teach the ownership doctrine from zero) — rejected: that is the Toaster song's and Lesson 1's job; this lane reports a fact and applies the doctrine to it.
records.context: STRUCT-2 re-audit (2026-10-24): H5 weak — APPLY in substance but never recorded; H4 weak — turn designed, schedule unrecorded. This record closes both.
records.why: An unrecorded role drifts: the next SoA piece inherits the stance only if it is written down.
records.change: A lane-level ruling that SoA pieces teach rather than report.

records.element: End referral — bridge card after the punchline (H6 / HS-06)
records.choice: A bridge compartment (no narration; the bed carries under it — CB-01) AFTER the L6 close (28.833→30.848s), in WD-01's bridge grammar: NEXT signpost → 'Renters can become owners.' → toaster symbol → 'WHO OWNS THE TOASTER?' → 'the song that asks who owns the layer' → 'tap to watch →'. Target: 'Who Owns the Toaster?', Hadosh Academy's song — THE FUNNEL long-form on the flagship channel, the piece that teaches the ownership question this report raises. T-18: the title is never dropped bare — the same card says what it is (a song) and what it asks (who owns the layer), in fresh words.
records.alternatives: (a) A spoken referral line — rejected: the narration is locked and the audio was never the defect (one-variable rule, DR-SCRIPT/DR-AUDIO). (b) Description/pinned-comment link only — rejected: it routes nobody from inside the piece; the audit calls the missing in-piece route the defect. (c) Referral inside the L6 frame — rejected: T-16, the close must land clean before the route is offered.
records.context: STRUCT-2 re-audit: H6 RANDOM-ABSENT — 'the script carries no end referral; the container end card carries only the series line + channel ask.' Objectives catalogue: 'the punchline routes nowhere… the cheapest alignment fix in the catalogue.' Funnel ruling: Toaster + Doorway are THE FUNNEL; shorts are judged by onward movement into them.
records.why: The objective ends at ownership; a viewer the punchline convinces is owed the route to the ownership teaching at the exact moment of conviction.
records.change: Funnel evidence (onward movement from this piece) against the bridge at the 48h scoreboard.

records.element: Audio — +2.000s bed extension at the outro boundary (SOA-FIX, 2026-10-24)
records.choice: The wrapped programme is extended by exactly 2.000s of the piece's OWN bed, spliced at the outro boundary (28.848s): head [0–28.848] + bed slice [26.848–28.848] taken from the wrapped music-only WAV (hidden_files/soa01/wrapped_audio.wav — corr 0.9957 with the main bed in the overlap window) + outro tail unchanged. 5ms edge micro-fades at the joins; narration, mix and mastering untouched; the AAC encode still happens exactly once, at render (A-09). The music-only twin programme receives the identical splice so the voice-swap pair stays in sync. Total 32.348 → 34.348s. Originals kept as *.pre-bridge.*.
records.alternatives: (a) Zero extension — rejected: the tail holds no spare room (narration ends 27.38s, the punchline holds to 28.833, the outro is a discrete 3.500s segment — RMS-verified); a bridge would have to eat the payoff hold or the container close. (b) A longer bridge (WD-01's 3.0s) — outside this job's ≤2s extension cap; 2.015s carries a signpost card, which is all a bridge is.
records.context: DR-AUDIO's 'bit-identical programme' claim is amended by this record for SOA-01 only; WD-01 is untouched. The extension exists solely to hold the DR-BRIDGE card over bed, as WD-01's bed-only bridge tail does.
records.why: The referral needs a readable hold; the bed extension buys it without touching a single spoken word or the mastered balance.
records.change: Nothing — a timing change to the outro segment itself would supersede this splice.
